notes: The margin's alternative rendering (a horn for his people, A praise for all his saints; Even for etc.) was read and set aside; the printed text governs under rule 38, so each lamed takes the of written for it, and the Hallelujah gloss on the closing name is set aside on the same terms.

Even introduces an appositive to his saints and no marker or conjunction stands on that phrase, so it is added under rules 16 and 30. Rule 16's *even unto* expansion was considered and does not reach it: that governs an extent or limit preposition, while this even stands before a nominal renaming what precedes, and the `לְ` beside it already holds the of written for it.

unto him is the suffix's as the rectum of the construct adjective under rule 19, headed on the pronoun. The competing reading treats unto as the valency of the predicate adjective under rule 33's closing paragraph; that paragraph governs a bare noun completing a predicate, and rule 19 states expressly that a pronominal suffix rectum changes nothing, its only exception being a governing word the ASV has written as an English verb, which near is not.
up is part of the English phrasal verb: `רוּם` hiphil is itself the raising high, so the particle restates what the Hebrew writes and rule 44's surplus test is not met.
